name: Narendra Modi
description: Indian prime minister associated with Hindu nationalism, infrastructure investment and economic and welfare reforms.
scope: Public positions and conduct during the specified period; this represents the individual rather than all party members or citizens.

axes.brief: Competitive elections continued while executive power and constraints on opposition expanded.
axes.counter: The 2024 election demonstrated real electoral competition; restrictions are not abolition of elections.

axes.brief: Security laws, communications restrictions and policing emphasised state order.
axes.counter: Constitutional protections and court review remained uneven rather than wholly absent.

axes.brief: Hindutva and common national identity prioritised majority traditions.
axes.counter: India’s institutional linguistic and religious diversity remained.

axes.brief: Citizenship policy selected particular persecuted religious groups and emphasised border control.
axes.counter: Naturalisation exceptions show selective protection rather than rejection of every refugee.

axes.brief: Cross-border strikes and defence capability supported national security priorities.
axes.counter: Diplomatic partnerships and restraint in some crises qualified force.

axes.brief: Strategic autonomy and national sovereignty coexisted with international partnerships.
axes.counter: Participation in multinational forums is not acceptance of binding supranational government.

axes.brief: Privatisation and business facilitation coexisted with large public enterprises.
axes.counter: Retained public banks and strategic firms qualify the private-preference estimates.

axes.brief: Domestic manufacturing and self-reliance initiatives used selective protection.
axes.counter: Foreign investment and export promotion were simultaneously encouraged.

axes.brief: Market reforms coexisted with government investment, incentives and national economic initiatives.
axes.counter: Demonetisation and sector intervention prevent a wholly laissez-faire reading.

axes.brief: Targeted benefits and financial inclusion coexisted with private enterprise and tax reform.
axes.counter: Targeted welfare does not imply strong income equalisation or no redistribution.

axes.brief: Public Hindu symbolism and religion-linked citizenship integrated faith into state politics.
axes.counter: Civil courts and legislation still functioned without a formal clerical veto.

axes.brief: Traditional social institutions coexisted with women’s participation and some welfare reforms.
axes.counter: Court-led rights changes cannot automatically be attributed to his personal endorsement.

axes.brief: Infrastructure, digital administration and industrial growth were prioritised.
axes.counter: Support for development does not demonstrate approval of risky enhancement medicine.

axes.brief: Central fiscal and security initiatives strengthened national authority, notably in Kashmir.
axes.counter: Cooperative federalism and devolved revenues supply counter-evidence.

axes.brief: Civilisational and cultural arguments coexist with education and opportunity policies.
axes.counter: Hindu nationalism does not settle heredity; no broad genetics doctrine was found.
axes.gap: Causal responses are especially provisional; cultural nationalism, faith and social tradition are not treated as biological evidence.
